Otoh why do you think that bills are going up.  Are you saying in quantity or in %? 

Quantity of total net issuance without regard to maturity is a function of

1) Total Deficit (obviously a need for funding but existing NET coupon debt issuance funds most of it)

3) Change in SOMA (currently static)

If in % that is a policy decision regarding how much coupon debt vs bills is chosen to be issued AND the feds reinvestment policy which could change.  
One upward pressure on bills AND some of the coupons is the buyback program which so far is a WAM decreasing pressure 

Bills dollar issuance is going up for sure due to deficit.  BIlls % is a different question 

Thoughts?

NFP - we had the best forecast for the third time in a row

Payrolls rose 29,000 against a consensus of 84-90,000, the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2%, and average hourly earnings came in at 0.1% on the month against 0.3% expected, 3.0% on the year. Our withheld-taxes model had a base case just south of 40k, so we were almost spot on again. That is the third correct NFP call in a row, and on the Bloomberg ranking it makes us the best of all forecasters over that stretch (pretty proud about that coming from a little shop in Copenhagen/London). Private payrolls rose 46,000 but government fell 17,000, education seasonals swung again, and the gains were concentrated in health care, construction and manufacturing while information, finance and energy shed jobs. Wage growth at 3.0% is not a number a central bank hikes on. The one soft spot in the soft read is that the unemployment rate rose partly because participation rose, which is a healthier reason than layoffs. The market took it the right way: October hike odds fell further, the front end rallied, the dollar gave back ground. Williams said one more and no rush. The data says maybe not even one.

Happy to agree to disagree, but you are a good guy with good takes so I am going to share my view (which I rarely do on CT these days)

I think SOL is kinda expensive on fundamentals today and its likely it will be cheaper against fundamentals in the future, while the price will still go up multiples

crypto cyclicality still seems to be a thing and we seem to be at the first leg of another crypto cycle (unless this time is different...)

while secular trends 1) tokenisation 2) trading volume moving on-chain are largely playing out as tailwind for SOL (judging by current backward facing metrics)

if these trends accelerate from linear to exponential growth, SOL price could grow and at the same time be "cheaper", because people suck at estimating and pricing in exponential growth

Kinda similar to Micron MU which went up 10x in a year and yet currently it's relative val is lower than a year ago (while half of the people argue its peak memory cycle and not sustainable, which is likely to happen for crypto as well...again)
